image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of an African crocodile (Nile crocodile) resting on a sandy bank. The image focuses primarily on the head and upper torso. The mouth is slightly open, revealing interlocking teeth. The skin texture is highly detailed, showing rough, bony scutes on the dorsal side and smoother, pale scales on the ventral jaw area. The eye is visible with a vertical slit pupil. There is a faint watermark or text artifact in the bottom left corner.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The snout tapers distinctly towards the nostrils, forming a V-shape characteristic of crocodiles rather than the U-shape of alligators. The head structure appears anatomically correct.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is slightly agape, clearly showing large, conical teeth. The fourth lower tooth appears to fit into the upper jaw notch, consistent with crocodile anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is positioned on top of the head. The pupil is a vertical slit. The nictitating membrane is not clearly deployed but the eye structure is intact and realistic.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Nostrils are clearly visible at the distal end of the snout, correctly positioned for a semi-aquatic reptile.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows heavy armor plating (scutes) and extends out of frame, implying an elongated form.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal skin exhibits complex, irregular but structured patterns of raised scutes typical of crocodilian osteoderms.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Coloration is greyish-brown with significant textural variation, matching the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside of the jaw and neck area shows significantly smoother, lighter-colored (off-white/pale grey) scales compared to the dorsal side.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The limbs are completely occluded by the body angle and framing; they are not visible in this crop.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is outside the frame of the image.

artifact_observations.reasoning: There is a faint, illegible string of characters or a watermark in the bottom left corner. It looks like degraded text or a signature, common in AI generations or scraped datasets, but does not disrupt the main subject.
Slight softness/bleeding where the lower jaw meets the sand, though this could also be depth-of-field blur. It lacks the crisp edge definition seen in the upper scutes.
